paragraphs: Predicting an agent’s future path requires understanding both movement over time and interactions with other agents. Learning those spatial and temporal patterns is difficult when trajectories are uncertain or distorted. This paper adds a self-supervised representation-learning task to existing trajectory predictors rather than replacing their prediction architecture.

Self-Supervised Waypoint Distortion Prediction, or SSWDP, trains the model to recognize distortions introduced into observed trajectories. Solving that auxiliary task encourages representations sensitive to meaningful trajectory structure. The authors present the approach as a complementary component that can improve several existing prediction methods.

On NBA, TrajNet++, and ETH-UCY, reported relative reductions in average and final displacement errors range from 16.60% to 38.9%. Gains are larger in some distorted-environment tests, reaching 76.8% and 82.5% for the two metrics on TrajNet++. These results support learning from synthetic distortions as a useful training signal, with the exact benefit depending on dataset, metric, and evaluation conditions.
icml-2024-enhancing-trajectory-predictio.tldr: Predicting synthetic waypoint distortions improves trajectory representations and reduces forecasting errors, especially in tested distorted environments.

paragraphs: An agent facing an unfamiliar partner or opponent must learn that peer’s behavior before responding effectively. Partial observability and long games make this identification problem difficult, because useful evidence may be spread across several interactions. This paper trains agents to explore specifically for information about their peers.

The proposed peer-identification reward measures how well the learning agent recognizes behavioral patterns from historical context, including observations across episodes. It encourages a context-aware policy to seek informative feedback when uncertain and exploit its accumulated understanding when confident. Exploration is therefore directed at distinguishing peer strategies, not just visiting unfamiliar states.

Experiments cover competitive Kuhn Poker, cooperative partially observable Overcooked, and a mixed predator–prey game. The method produces more active exploration, faster adaptation, and better outcomes than the compared approaches. The contribution is an explicit learning signal for social adaptation, with evidence spanning different interaction types rather than a single fixed cooperative task.
icml-2024-fast-peer-adaptation-with-cont.tldr: A peer-identification reward teaches agents to gather useful behavioral evidence and adapt faster to unfamiliar partners or opponents.

paragraphs: A confidence sequence provides uncertainty sets that remain valid across time, allowing an analyst to inspect accumulating data without committing to a single stopping point. This paper extends gambling-based constructions from scalar bounded observations to bounded random vectors. The target is the mean of a multivariate stochastic process.

The framework gives constructions for categorical observations and probability vectors, plus a reduction for general bounded multidimensional data. The authors examine mixture-portfolio strategies analogous to Cover’s universal portfolio. These betting strategies determine confidence sets through the statistical guarantees attached to their accumulated performance.

Simulations show tighter confidence sequences than existing methods. For sampling finite categorical data without replacement, the universal-gambling construction is provably tighter than a particular posterior-prior-ratio martingale method. The contribution combines a general multivariate recipe with stronger results in that specific sampling setting; the abstract does not establish that every portfolio choice dominates every alternative confidence sequence.
icml-2024-gambling-based-confidence-sequ.tldr: A multivariate gambling framework builds time-valid confidence sequences, with tight empirical and without-replacement guarantees.

paragraphs: Feature selection can reduce the cost of collecting high-dimensional data, but jointly learning selected features and a decoder can be unstable. This paper identifies a connection between that instability in Concrete Autoencoders and the repeated selection of the same feature. It proposes a small change in how the selection distributions are parameterized.

Indirectly Parameterized Concrete Autoencoders learn an embedding and a mapping from that embedding to the parameters of Gumbel–softmax distributions. This indirect representation changes the optimization of feature choices while retaining a neural embedded-selection framework. The approach can exploit nonlinear relationships and does not require separately retraining the jointly optimized decoder.

Across reconstruction and classification datasets, IP-CAE consistently improves generalization and training time relative to standard CAE. The authors also suggest that the parameterization principle could extend beyond feature selection. That broader possibility is a methodological implication, while the concrete empirical evidence reported in the abstract concerns the evaluated feature-selection tasks.
icml-2024-indirectly-parameterized-concr.tldr: Indirect parameterization stabilizes Concrete Autoencoder feature selection and improves training speed and generalization in the reported tests.

paragraphs: Language-model inference first processes the prompt before generating its initial output token. For long prompts, this prefill phase can become a major latency source even though later decoding benefits from a key-value cache. KV-Runahead reuses that caching structure to parallelize prompt processing itself.

The method coordinates multiple processes to populate the cache, using causal attention structure to organize the work. It also introduces context-level load balancing because different portions of the prompt require unequal cache-generation effort. The intended outcome is a shorter time to first token through a parallelization strategy compatible with mechanisms already used during decoding.

Compared with existing tensor or sequence parallelization approaches, the experiments show speedups above 1.4 times for Llama 7B and 1.6 times for Falcon 7B. The contribution specifically concerns accelerating the prompt phase. Those measurements should not be interpreted as an identical improvement in every subsequent decoding step or in all end-to-end serving workloads.
icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.tldr: KV-Runahead parallelizes key-value cache generation during prefill to reduce language-model time to first token.

paragraphs: Local feature selection explains a prediction by showing a small set of relevant inputs. But the pattern of selected features can itself encode extra information, making an apparently sparse explanation misleading. This paper formalizes that issue as label leakage and feature leakage within the selection process.

The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for avoiding leakage and show that existing methods fail those conditions. They then introduce SUWR, a local feature-selection method with a proof of no leakage. The formal framework is intended to support reliable explanations by ensuring the selection mechanism does not secretly communicate information beyond the selected values.

Experiments find less overfitting and a combination of strong predictive performance with sparse selections. The contribution is therefore both a diagnostic theory and a method satisfying it. The no-leakage property addresses a specific failure mode in feature-based explanations; it does not by itself certify that every selected feature is causally responsible for the underlying outcome.
icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.tldr: SUWR provides provably leakage-free local feature selection, making sparse prediction explanations less prone to hidden information encoding.

paragraphs: Combining data from several sources can improve prediction, but distribution shifts make uncertainty estimates for a target population difficult. Privacy constraints may also limit access to individual records. This paper develops prediction intervals that use potentially biased sources while accounting for differences between them.

The authors derive efficient influence functions for relevant outcome quantiles and allow machine-learning methods to estimate nuisance functions while retaining parametric convergence rates to nominal coverage. When conditional outcome invariance fails, an adaptive weighting strategy emphasizes informative sources and reduces the contribution of less useful sources to manage bias and efficiency.

Synthetic experiments examine different conformal scores and data-generating mechanisms. An application constructs hospital-length-of-stay intervals for pediatric patients undergoing high-risk cardiac surgery in the United States. The contribution is uncertainty quantification for multi-source prediction; its coverage and efficiency statements depend on the paper’s estimation conditions, rather than assuming that pooling heterogeneous datasets automatically produces valid intervals.
icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.tldr: Multi-source conformal inference uses influence-function estimation and adaptive source weights to improve target-population prediction intervals.

paragraphs: A learning agent often must maximize reward while meeting requirements accumulated over time, such as a spending or resource constraint. This paper studies episodic constrained Markov decision processes with unknown transitions. Both rewards and constraints may be generated stochastically or chosen adversarially, making the learning environment especially flexible.

The proposed algorithm handles these regimes without knowing which process generated the observations. Its best-of-both-worlds design aims to retain strong behavior under benign stochastic conditions while providing guarantees when constraints or rewards are adversarial. Long-term constraint control is part of the learning objective, rather than a requirement checked only after a policy has been trained.

For stochastic constraints, the method matches existing regret and constraint-violation bounds. The authors also provide the first guarantees in the studied adversarial-constraint setting. The contribution is theoretical coverage across these environments; long-term violation bounds should not be mistaken for a statement that every individual action satisfies every possible safety constraint.
icml-2024-online-learning-in-cmdps-handl.tldr: A best-of-both-worlds CMDP algorithm controls regret and long-term violations under stochastic or adversarial rewards and constraints.

paragraphs: Using AI to support public policy requires more than optimizing a fixed technical objective. Economic environments involve interacting participants, and the objectives themselves may need collective input. This position paper proposes Social Environment Design as a framework and research agenda for studying those issues together.

The framework connects reinforcement learning, economics and computation, and computational social choice. It aims to represent general economic environments, include voting over policy objectives, and support systematic analysis through AI simulation. This places both the design of the social environment and the selection of desired outcomes within the scope of the research program.

The paper highlights open problems rather than presenting a completed policy-making system or an empirical demonstration of improved governance. Its intended contribution is to organize future work toward social-welfare goals and more responsible decision-making. Assessing a real policy would still require addressing the framework’s unresolved modeling, objective-selection, and analysis challenges.
icml-2024-position-social-environment-de.tldr: Social Environment Design proposes a research framework linking AI simulation, economic environments, and collective choice of policy objectives.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation can improve accuracy on an unlabeled target domain while leaving confidence estimates poorly calibrated. Calibration is difficult because the target labels needed for conventional methods are unavailable and the domains may differ substantially. PseudoCal treats this as a target-specific unsupervised calibration problem.

The method uses inference-stage mixup to construct a labeled pseudo-target dataset intended to reflect the structure of the actual target examples. This converts the calibration step into a supervised problem on the synthesized data, where temperature scaling can be applied. It is a post-hoc framework rather than a requirement to redesign the adaptation algorithm itself.

Across five adaptation scenarios and ten UDA methods, the experiments show consistently stronger calibration than existing alternatives. The contribution is a practical route to confidence adjustment without labeled target data. Its effectiveness rests on how well the pseudo-target construction supports calibration in the evaluated settings; the abstract does not state a distribution-free calibration guarantee.
icml-2024-pseudo-calibration-improving-p.tldr: PseudoCal synthesizes a pseudo-target calibration set with mixup, enabling temperature scaling without labeled target examples.

paragraphs: Long-context language-model decoding can be limited by loading a large key-value cache for attention. Only a subset of past tokens may strongly affect a given attention output, but that subset changes with the current query. Quest exploits this query dependence to select useful cache pages dynamically.

The algorithm stores minimum and maximum key values for each cache page and uses the query vector to estimate that page’s importance. Attention then loads only the top-ranked pages. This reduces cache traffic while preserving the ability to retrieve different parts of the context for different queries.

The abstract reports up to 2.23-fold self-attention speedup and 7.03-fold inference-latency reduction, with negligible accuracy loss on evaluated long-dependency tasks. Those figures describe reported performance measures and should not be conflated into a single universal speedup. The contribution is a lightweight, query-aware selection mechanism that makes sparse cache access responsive to the current computation.
icml-2024-quest-query-aware-sparsity-for.tldr: Quest ranks KV-cache pages using each attention query, reducing long-context inference cost with little reported accuracy loss.

paragraphs: Comparing language models on safety-related metrics often compresses variable outcomes into single averages. This paper proposes a distributional framework that compares risk while quantifying statistical significance. The goal is to support model selection when several guardrail metrics and their uncertainty matter together.

The authors develop relative tests based on first- and second-order stochastic dominance. They connect second-order behavior to mean-risk decision models and aggregate collections of metrics into a portfolio for each model. Model selection then compares these portfolios, drawing on ideas from financial portfolio optimization without treating all risk measures as interchangeable.

An asymptotic analysis provides significance guarantees, with bootstrap variance estimates used in practice. Applications compare language models on instruction drift and toxic output. The contribution is a statistical decision framework for benchmark results; conclusions still depend on the selected metrics and their aggregation, rather than constituting an all-purpose ranking of model safety.
icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.tldr: Risk-aware benchmarking compares distributions of metric portfolios with statistical significance instead of relying only on average scores.

paragraphs: Weight decay changes more than the size of neural-network weights: it also affects how their directions evolve during training. This paper studies those dynamics at the level of individual neurons. It introduces rotational equilibrium, a steady state in the expected magnitude and angular size of weight updates.

Through analysis and experiments with Adam, Lion, and momentum SGD, the authors show that these equilibria can balance average rotation across layers and neurons. Rotation serves as a proxy for effective learning rate. This perspective helps explain the benefits of Weight Standardization and differences between AdamW and Adam with an L2 penalty.

The paper also finds that explicitly controlling rotation can retain benefits associated with weight decay while substantially reducing the need for learning-rate warmup. The contribution is a mechanism connecting familiar optimization choices to balanced update behavior. It does not imply that weight decay has only one effect or that the same equilibrium holds identically for every training configuration.
icml-2024-rotational-equilibrium-how-wei.tldr: Weight decay can balance neuron-wise angular updates, explaining optimization benefits and motivating explicit rotation control.

paragraphs: Deep Gaussian processes use sparse inducing variables to make Bayesian inference computationally manageable. Approximating their posterior remains difficult, and restrictive variational methods can introduce substantial bias. This paper proposes a diffusion-based alternative for representing that posterior more flexibly.

Denoising Diffusion Variational Inference generates posterior samples through a denoising diffusion stochastic differential equation. A neural network approximates the required score functions using score-matching ideas. The authors combine SDE theory with minimization of a divergence between approximate and true processes to derive an explicit variational lower bound for the model’s marginal likelihood.

Experiments across several datasets compare DDVI with baseline inference methods and support its effectiveness for deep Gaussian processes. The contribution is an inference procedure and training bound, rather than a change to the basic meaning of the model’s observations. The abstract does not quantify how much posterior bias remains or establish exact posterior sampling in finite training.
icml-2024-sparse-inducing-points-in-deep.tldr: Diffusion-based variational inference provides a flexible posterior sampler and explicit training bound for sparse deep Gaussian processes.

paragraphs: Some continuous-time adversarial games combine physical constraints with private information. One player may know its payoff type while the opponent only maintains a belief about it. This paper studies such zero-sum differential games when the informed player must also avoid violating state constraints.

The authors extend an earlier value-existence and belief-convexity result to the constrained setting. They derive primal and dual subdynamic principles needed to compute behavioral strategies. The analysis reveals how private information, belief manipulation, and state constraints jointly shape strategic behavior, rather than treating deception and physical feasibility as separate problems.

A simplified football matchup illustrates the theory. The computed strategies identify positions and beliefs where randomized deceptive moves are useful, as well as the defender’s response. The contribution supplies structure for future scalable learning in continuous-action, long-horizon games; the abstract does not present a general-purpose scalable learning system for every such game.
icml-2024-state-constrained-zero-sum-dif.tldr: A theory of constrained differential games explains how private information and belief manipulation shape continuous-time strategies.

paragraphs: A coordinated group can influence a machine-learning system through collective action involving its data. Prior analyses often evaluated that influence against idealized Bayes classifiers. This paper argues that real learning algorithms have their own biases, which can materially change how much influence a collective achieves.

The authors focus on distributionally robust optimization and stochastic gradient descent. The former is motivated by improving worst-group error, while the latter has a preference for simpler functions. They investigate how these algorithmic properties affect both the effective size of a collective and the success of its attempted influence.

Empirical results, supported by theoretical analysis, show strong dependence on the learning algorithm. The contribution is to make algorithm choice an explicit part of collective-action analysis instead of assuming that all sufficiently accurate classifiers respond similarly. The abstract does not specify a universal direction of the effect; whether a collective gains influence depends on the relevant algorithmic properties and setting.
icml-2024-the-role-of-learning-algorithm.tldr: The success of collective influence on machine learning depends strongly on the learning algorithm and its inductive biases.

paragraphs: A classifier can recognize an object in one orientation yet fail after a spatial transformation. Training-time augmentation and built-in architectural invariances address this problem, but both have limits. This paper instead studies whether inference can actively transform the input to expose recognition ability already present in a model.

Inverse Transformation Search traverses a sparse tree of inverse transformations using parallel energy-based evaluations. The procedure is model-agnostic and operates during inference. It aims to provide zero-shot pseudo-invariance, meaning improved behavior on transformed inputs without requiring the classifier to have been trained specifically for those test transformations.

Tests include several benchmarks and a synthesized ImageNet test set. ITS outperforms the selected baselines in all reported zero-shot scenarios. The contribution is an inference-time search strategy for spatial robustness; pseudo-invariance is a performance objective here, not a proof of exact invariance to every possible transformation or a guarantee of zero additional inference cost.
icml-2024-tilt-your-head-activating-the-.tldr: Inverse Transformation Search improves spatial robustness by exploring input transformations during inference without task-specific retraining.

paragraphs: Text watermarking modifies language-model generation so an automated detector can later recognize a statistical marker. Stronger markers can improve detection but may damage the meaning or fluency of the text. This paper treats that tension as a multi-objective optimization problem.

The proposed method uses lightweight networks to produce token-specific watermarking logits and splitting ratios. Its objectives explicitly address both detection and semantic quality, allowing the watermarking behavior to vary across tokens. The intended effect is to place detectable structure into generated text while preserving coherence rather than applying one uniform adjustment everywhere.

Experiments show better detectability than current watermarking methods while maintaining semantic coherence. The contribution is an adaptive generation-time watermark with an explicit quality objective. The abstract does not establish that every generated passage is detectable after arbitrary editing, nor that a detector can always distinguish all human and model writing; its claims concern the evaluated watermarking comparison.
icml-2024-token-specific-watermarking-wi.tldr: Token-specific multi-objective watermarking improves detection while preserving the reported semantic quality of generated text.

paragraphs: Theoretical studies of in-context learning had largely examined a single attention layer on linear regression tasks. This paper adds a learned nonlinear feature map, bringing the analyzed model closer to a mechanism that can reuse representations across tasks. The architecture consists of a fully connected layer followed by linear attention.

In the mean-field and two-timescale limit, the authors study the loss landscape over distributions of parameters. Although nonconvex, that landscape has favorable structure. They analyze second-order stability and show that the associated Wasserstein gradient flow almost always avoids saddle points, addressing whether optimization can move beyond unhelpful stationary behavior.

The paper also derives concrete improvement rates both near and away from critical points. Its contribution combines a nonlinear representation account of in-context learning with new tools for mean-field optimization. The guarantees concern the specified limiting model and dynamics, rather than establishing identical behavior for every finite Transformer or language-model training setup.
icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.tldr: A mean-field analysis shows favorable optimization dynamics for Transformers that learn nonlinear features for in-context learning.

paragraphs: Choosing a step-size schedule for stochastic optimization often requires knowing both how noisy gradients are and how smooth the objective is. This paper develops methods that adapt to those properties without prior knowledge. The setting is convex optimization across the full Hölder smoothness class, including nonsmooth objectives.

The Universal Gradient Method adjusts step-size coefficients using combinations of gradient differences and iterate differences. This differs from accumulating gradient norms as in AdaGrad. The update rule uses information about how the optimization process changes locally to adapt its behavior to the objective and the stochastic oracle.

The resulting guarantees match state-of-the-art worst-case convergence rates throughout the studied smoothness class. The authors also introduce a Universal Fast Gradient Method with optimal efficiency estimates. The contribution is adaptive optimization with broad theoretical coverage; those guarantees rely on convexity and the stated oracle setting, rather than extending automatically to arbitrary nonconvex neural-network training.
icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.tldr: Universal gradient methods adapt to unknown noise and Hölder smoothness while retaining strong stochastic convex-optimization guarantees.

paragraphs: Animals are often taught complex tasks through shaping: a curriculum that first develops simpler component skills. The choice of curriculum can determine whether learning is fast, slow, or unsuccessful. This paper builds a theoretical model to explain when component pretraining helps with a later compositional task.

The authors analyze deep policy-gradient learning in a class of simple compositional reinforcement-learning problems. Statistical-physics tools yield exact learning dynamics for the model. This makes it possible to compare strategies such as learning primitives individually before combining them, rather than judging curricula only through trial and error.

The analysis reveals an interaction between task complexity and the effectiveness of shaping strategies. It gives a quantitative account of how training protocols expose useful primitives and can produce faster, more robust learning. The contribution is an explanatory theory for the studied task class, not a complete account of animal learning or a universal curriculum prescription for all reinforcement-learning problems.
icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.tldr: Exact learning dynamics in a compositional RL model explain when training component skills first improves later task learning.

paragraphs: Text-guided avatar generation aims to turn a verbal description into a usable three-dimensional character, but existing methods can produce oversaturated textures and low-quality outputs. X-Oscar addresses those problems through a staged generation process. It also targets avatars that can be animated, rather than only static 3D assets.

The framework proceeds from geometry to texture and then animation, simplifying optimization by separating successive stages. Adaptive Variational Parameter represents the avatar as an adaptive distribution during training to address oversaturation. Avatar-aware Score Distillation Sampling adds avatar-aware noise to rendered images to improve the optimization signal and generation quality.

Extensive evaluations show advantages over existing text-to-3D and text-to-avatar approaches. The contribution combines a progressive pipeline with two training modifications tailored to avatar generation. The abstract does not specify evaluation scores, motion-quality measures, or computational cost, so its reported superiority should be interpreted within the paper’s evaluated methods and settings.
icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.tldr: X-Oscar progressively generates geometry, texture, and animation while using avatar-specific optimization to improve text-guided 3D characters.

paragraphs: Systems with access to several language models can trade output quality against cost. Routing chooses one model for a query, while cascading can try additional models until a satisfactory result is obtained. This paper develops a common theoretical treatment and asks when each approach is useful.

The authors derive an optimal cascading strategy and prove optimality of an existing routing strategy. They then introduce cascade routing, which combines the two into a unified optimal strategy under their framework. The analysis identifies reliable quality estimators as a central requirement: selecting models effectively depends on predicting which outputs are worth their cost.

Experiments show that cascade routing substantially and consistently outperforms the individual approaches in the evaluated comparisons. The paper also analyzes estimators to characterize conditions favoring routing or cascading. The optimality statements belong to the formulated decision problem and its assumptions, rather than guaranteeing that any practical quality predictor yields an optimal real-world deployment.
icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.tldr: Cascade routing unifies model selection and sequential escalation, with quality estimation determining the achievable cost–performance benefit.

paragraphs: A model can waste computation when its capacity exceeds what the data support, but too little capacity can limit accuracy. Continual learning makes this choice harder because the final amount of data is unknown. This paper studies how to adjust Gaussian-process model size as observations arrive incrementally.

The proposed method changes model size automatically while maintaining near-optimal performance. It focuses on avoiding a fixed capacity chosen from advance knowledge of the dataset, such as a predetermined number of inducing points. This makes the size decision part of the continual-learning procedure rather than a one-time configuration based on a completed dataset.

Experiments enforce that hyperparameters are chosen without observing dataset properties. Under that constraint, the method works across diverse datasets without retuning its hyperparameter, demonstrating reduced tuning needs relative to alternatives. The contribution is adaptive capacity management for continual Gaussian processes; the abstract does not provide the detailed rule or a universal numerical threshold for when additional capacity stops helping.
icml-2025-adjusting-model-size-in-contin.tldr: An adaptive model-size method lets continual Gaussian processes grow as needed without dataset-specific capacity tuning.

paragraphs: Evaluating a machine-learning model usually requires labeled validation examples, and obtaining reliable human labels can be slow and expensive. Autoevaluation uses AI-labeled synthetic data to reduce that burden. The key statistical challenge is to gain efficiency without systematically distorting the estimated model performance.

This paper proposes algorithms for combining synthetic evaluation information with the goal of reducing required human annotation. The abstract emphasizes two properties: statistical principledness and unbiasedness. That combination matters because a large supply of inexpensive synthetic labels is useful only if the resulting evaluation still targets the intended performance quantity reliably.

The stated result is improved sample efficiency while remaining unbiased. The abstract does not describe the estimators, experiments, assumptions, or size of the efficiency gain, so those details require consulting the source. Its contribution is narrowly an evaluation methodology; it does not claim that synthetic labels are universally correct or that human validation can always be eliminated.
icml-2025-autoeval-done-right-using-synt.tldr: Statistically principled autoevaluation uses synthetic data to reduce human-label requirements while keeping performance estimates unbiased.
